- Model consistently underestimates true values, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecast tends to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually increases — suggesting a lag or delayed response to recent price trends.
- After sharp spikes in history (e.g., 85+), model overreacts with exaggerated upward forecasts, then corrects too late — leading to overshoot followed by sharp drop.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to pull prices back toward historical averages after volatility spikes.
- Forecast horizon 30d exhibits persistent bias toward lower values, especially when history includes recent high prices — model underweights recent momentum.
- Model often misses the “tail” of the price distribution — underestimates late-period true values, particularly in the final 5–10 days of the forecast.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model forecasts a steeper rise than observed — overestimates momentum.
- Model tends to ignore recent low prices in history when forecasting — underweights downward momentum, leading to overestimation of future prices.
